therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: glucose-dependent insulin secretion and glycemic control
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: hyperglycemic patients admitted to coronary ICU with acute coronary syndromes or myocardial infarction
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: median glucose values from steady state through 48 hours; time to steady state (first glucose ≤140 mg/dL)

results.effect_size: Median glucose 132 mg/dL (95% CI 110–157); time to steady state 2.0 hours (95% CI 1.5–5.0)
biomarker_changes: Median glucose from steady state through 48 hours: 132 mg/dL for exenatide vs 127 mg/dL (moderate insulin) vs 105 mg/dL (intensive insulin)
Time to steady state: 2.0 hours for exenatide vs 12.0 hours (moderate insulin) vs 3.0 hours (intensive insulin)
subgroup_findings: Patients with at least one hypoglycemic episode (BG <70 mg/dL): exenatide 4, moderate insulin 14, intensive insulin 22
Patients with at least one severe hypoglycemic episode (BG <50 mg/dL): exenatide 0, moderate insulin 2, intensive insulin 1
safety_signals: 4 serious adverse events in exenatide arm over 30 days: 3 deaths and 1 stroke
No severe hypoglycemia (BG <50 mg/dL) in exenatide arm
Lower rates of hypoglycemia compared to insulin arms

dose_info.dose: 0.05 µg/min bolus followed by 0.025 µg/min infusion
dose_info.schedule: bolus then constant infusion for 24–48 hours

context.indication: hyperglycemia in acute coronary syndromes / myocardial infarction
context.comparator: moderate insulin infusion; intensive insulin infusion
context.duration: 24–48 hours treatment; 30-day follow-up for serious adverse events

subgroups.raw_descriptor: Patients with at least one hypoglycemic episode
